source.title: From Parameters to Performance: A Data-Driven Study on LLM Structure and Development
source.authors: Suqing Wang; Z. Li; Luo-He Shi; Bo Du; Hai Zhao; Yun Li; Qian-Ren Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure text is garbled in the extracted text, but the relevant regression table is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether downstream benchmark performance can be predicted from model size and other structural features using regression, but does not measure pretraining loss or reproduce a controlled scaling-law experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling laws but does not test held-out cross-entropy loss, power-law fits, small-run extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation. Its relevant original results are regression R2 scores for predicting benchmark performance from structural features. Other numerical results and pruning analyses address structural effects but do not test the versions as stated.
record.test_reason: Section 3 and Figure 5 directly examine downstream benchmark scores against parameter count, finding a generally positive relationship with a dip at 10B–20B. This bears on V6. Table 2 instead compares multifeature prediction methods; its R2 scores do not establish that performance improves predictably with scale.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors identify model size and release date as primary performance correlates, report the strongest predictive fits from Random Forest, and argue that depth and FFN width have task-dependent roles. They use pruning and gradient analyses to corroborate these structural interpretations and present the findings as guidance for model design.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cross-sectional regression on model structures and downstream leaderboard scores, rather than controlled language-model training sweeps and held-out cross-entropy loss measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Predictive R2 varies by regression method and benchmark; the authors report Random Forest as the strongest method.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports R2 values of 17%–81% for predicting benchmark scores jointly from structural and other model features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream benchmark scores are partly predictable from multiple model attributes, with predictive fit varying by regression method and task.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The relevant results are observational predictions from a heterogeneous model dataset and do not isolate model size from other structural features or release date. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the R2 scores. The paper notes its task coverage is limited.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit is filled by all Table 2 method-by-benchmark R2 results. Not extracted: the additional specialized-task regression results and feature-importance results in Table 3 and Section 4, plus figure-only model-size trends and pruning/gradient analyses in Figures 5, 9, 10, and 15–17. Those results do not test the stated scaling-law versions; the pruning results concern downstream task sensitivity to depth, not fixed-parameter-count loss.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss, power-law form, and scaling across several orders of magnitude.
Small-run power-law fits predicting much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its scaling exponents.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count measuring pretraining loss; pruning changes parameter count and measures downstream scores.
Power-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
Prediction from pretraining loss; quantitative scale-only predictive accuracy, controlled training sweeps, and extrapolation to larger scales.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 5 is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not listed as an undeclared missing result. Its relevance to V6 was incorrectly dismissed there. The V6 verdicts use its explicit textual description; exact bin scores cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied figure text. Table 2 values are transcribed correctly, but its prediction-method comparisons should not substitute for scale-effect rows. No reported R2 threshold justifies the record's observed/partial classifications.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law form and several-orders-of-magnitude range.
No power-law fits on small runs or predictions of much larger runs.
No compute-budget comparison or measurement of optimal parameter/token allocation.
No fixed-parameter-count architecture comparison measuring held-out loss; pruning tests downstream benchmark scores and changes parameter count.
No tests of power laws in other modalities or training regimes.
The regressions predict downstream benchmark scores from multiple structural features; they do not isolate scale alone or test prediction from pretraining loss.
No fitting of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits, and no analysis of fit choices or curves bending away from power laws.

relationships.condition: Overall cross-sectional model-size trends across the six leaderboard benchmarks
relationships.reason: Section 3's discussion of Figure 5 reports generally increasing benchmark performance with parameter count; this is qualitative observational support from the text, outside the extracted rows.
relationships.display_finding: The study reported generally increasing benchmark performance with parameter count across the six benchmarks.

relationships.reason: Section 3 explicitly reports a performance dip in Figure 5, qualifying a uniformly improving scale relationship; this verdict rests on the text, outside the extracted rows.
relationships.display_finding: The reported performance dip contradicted a uniformly increasing relationship between model size and performance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Random Forest regression across the six leaderboard benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The reported R2 scores range from 58% to 81%, showing predictive signal from structural parameters; see r01–r06.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Other tested regression methods and benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Predictive fit varies by method and benchmark, with several R2 scores modest and LLM Fine-tune reaching 17% on TruthfulQA; see r07–r60.
